items.value: Only four of the five listed countries have more than four time zones — the United Kingdom, Denmark, New Zealand and Australia; Brazil has exactly four
items.reasoning: Counting overseas territories and dependencies, the United Kingdom spans about nine time zones (Pitcairn UTC-8 through the British Indian Ocean Territory UTC+6) and Australia about nine (Christmas and Cocos Islands, Western, Central, Eastern, Lord Howe, Norfolk, Macquarie, Heard & McDonald). Denmark has five (Denmark UTC+1, the Faroes UTC+0, and three zones across Greenland including Pituffik/Thule), and New Zealand five (NZST UTC+12, Chatham UTC+12:45, Cook Islands UTC-10, Niue UTC-11, Tokelau UTC+13). Brazil has exactly four — Acre UTC-5, Amazon UTC-4, Brasilia UTC-3 and Fernando de Noronha UTC-2 — so it fails the strict 'more than four' test, leaving four qualifying countries.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — the two towns lie on opposite sides of the International Date Line so their breakfast hours fall on different dates, but statement II reverses the direction
items.reasoning: Anadyr in Chukotka keeps UTC+12 while Nome in Alaska keeps UTC-9, and the International Date Line runs between them, so Anadyr is about 21 hours ahead and the two towns are on different calendar dates through most of the day — statement I's point about breakfast falling on different days holds. Statement II inverts this: Anadyr is the town that is ahead, so when it is Monday in Anadyr it is Sunday (not Tuesday) in Nome. Note that statement I's claim that the two are 'a few kilometers' apart is geographically loose — Anadyr and Nome are roughly 800 km apart, and it is Big Diomede and Little Diomede that lie a few kilometres apart across the Date Line — but the statement's substantive claim about different days is the one being tested and it is sound.

items.value: 'Periyar' E. V. Ramaswamy Naicker founded the Self-Respect Movement
items.reasoning: E. V. Ramaswamy Naicker, known as Periyar, launched the Self-Respect Movement (Suyamariyathai Iyakkam) in Tamil Nadu in 1925 after leaving the Congress, campaigning against Brahminical dominance, caste hierarchy and priest-led ritual, and promoting self-respect marriages. Ambedkar led the parallel but separate anti-caste movement in Maharashtra, while Bhaskarrao Jadhav and Dinkarrao Javalkar were non-Brahmin/Satyashodhak leaders in Maharashtra, not founders of this movement.

items.value: All three pairs are correctly matched — Botswana with diamond, Chile with lithium and Indonesia with nickel
items.reasoning: Botswana is among the world's leading diamond producers by value, with the Jwaneng and Orapa mines run by Debswana. Chile sits in the 'lithium triangle' and draws lithium from brine at the Salar de Atacama, ranking among the top producers and holding the largest reserves. Indonesia is the world's largest nickel producer, supplying roughly half of global output from Sulawesi and Halmahera. All three rows therefore match.

items.value: Both statements are correct and the phosphorescent property of rare earths is the reason they are used in flat screens
items.reasoning: Rare earth elements such as europium, terbium, yttrium and cerium are used as phosphors in flat television screens and computer monitors, so Statement I is correct. Statement II is also correct — these elements luminesce in characteristic colours when excited, which is exactly the property being exploited (europium compounds give red, terbium green). Because the display application depends directly on that luminescent behaviour, Statement II explains Statement I, making A rather than B the right choice; the judgement call here is only whether the explanatory link is direct enough, and it is, since the phosphor is the whole reason the element is in the screen.

items.value: Statements I and II are the ones that are not correct — the National Rail Plan targets 2030 rather than 2028, and Kavach is an indigenous system, not a German collaboration
items.reasoning: The National Rail Plan is framed as NRP-2030 and sets out to create a 'future ready' railway system by 2030, so the 2028 date in statement I is wrong. Kavach is an Automatic Train Protection system developed indigenously by RDSO with Indian industry partners and certified to SIL-4; it was not developed in collaboration with Germany, so statement II is wrong. Statement III is correct — RFID tags fitted on the track in station and block sections give the locomotive its absolute location reference. Since the question asks which are NOT correct, the set must contain II and exclude III, and option A is the only one that does.

items.value: All three missions encourage and support micro-gravity research
items.reasoning: Axiom-4 carried Indian astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla to the International Space Station along with a suite of ISRO micro-gravity experiments, so it clearly qualifies. Gaganyaan, India's human spaceflight programme, is explicitly intended to enable micro-gravity experiments in low Earth orbit. SpaDeX is the borderline case: its headline objective is autonomous docking, but the mission's PSLV-C60 POEM-4 platform hosted micro-gravity payloads including CROPS, the seed-germination experiment that sprouted leaves in orbit, and docking capability is itself the prerequisite for the planned Indian space station's micro-gravity work. Read against the deliberately broad wording 'encourage and support', all three qualify; a narrower reading that treats SpaDeX as a pure technology demonstrator would give 'only two'.

items.value: Only two pairs match — Dornier-228 as a maritime patrol aircraft and C-17 Globemaster III as a military transport; the IL-76 is a heavy transport, not a supersonic combat aircraft
items.reasoning: The Dornier-228 is flown by the Indian Navy and Coast Guard for maritime patrol and coastal surveillance, so row I matches. The C-17 Globemaster III is the Indian Air Force's heavy-lift strategic airlifter, so row III matches. The Ilyushin IL-76 is a four-engine subsonic heavy transport (and the basis of the IAF's tanker and AEW&C platforms); calling it a supersonic combat aircraft is wrong, so row II fails and the count is two.

items.value: Cloud seeding to induce artificial rain uses silver iodide and potassium iodide
items.reasoning: Artificial rain is produced by cloud seeding, in which silver iodide and potassium iodide (often with dry ice) are dispersed into moisture-bearing clouds. Both iodides have a crystal lattice closely resembling that of ice, so they act as ice nuclei around which supercooled droplets freeze and grow heavy enough to fall. Nitrates and chlorides do not provide this ice-nucleating lattice, which rules out options B, C and D.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — the pardoning power is open to limited judicial review, but the President must act on ministerial advice
items.reasoning: The Supreme Court has held, notably in Epuru Sudhakar v. Government of Andhra Pradesh (2006), that an order under Article 72 is amenable to limited judicial review on grounds such as mala fides, arbitrariness, non-application of mind or reliance on irrelevant or extraneous material, so statement I is correct. Statement II is wrong: the President exercises the pardoning power on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers under Article 74(1), as settled in Maru Ram v. Union of India (1980) and Kehar Singh v. Union of India (1989); it is not a personal discretion exercised independently of the government.

items.value: Statements I and III are correct — the Speaker continues in office until just before the first meeting of the new House, and removal requires a majority of all then members after fourteen days' notice; statement II is not a constitutional requirement
items.reasoning: Article 94 provides that on dissolution of the House of the People the Speaker does not vacate office until immediately before the first meeting of the House after the dissolution, so statement I is correct. The same article requires that removal be by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, with a proviso that no such resolution may be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given, so statement III is correct. Statement II is wrong — resigning from one's party on election as Speaker is a British convention that India has never adopted, and the Constitution contains no such provision.

items.value: Neither statement is correct — anti-defection questions are decided by the Speaker, not the President, and the Constitution does use the expression 'political party'
items.reasoning: Under paragraph 6 of the Tenth Schedule, a question of disqualification on ground of defection is decided by the Chairman or Speaker of the House concerned, whose decision is final; the President-on-Election-Commission-opinion route of Articles 103 and 192 expressly does not cover the Tenth Schedule, and there is no role at all for the Council of Ministers, so statement I is wrong. Statement II is wrong on its face, because the Tenth Schedule inserted by the Fifty-second Amendment repeatedly uses the words 'political party' — for instance in defining the original political party of a member and in the provisions on merger.

items.value: Statement I is not correct but Statement II is — States do have rule-making power over minor mineral concessions, while the Centre has the power to notify minor minerals
items.reasoning: Section 15 of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 expressly empowers State Governments to make rules for regulating the grant of quarry leases, mining leases and other mineral concessions in respect of minor minerals, so Statement I is factually wrong. Statement II is correct: section 3(e) of the same Act, after listing building stones, gravel, ordinary clay and ordinary sand, allows the Central Government to declare any other mineral to be a minor mineral by notification in the Official Gazette. The correct description is therefore that the first statement is wrong and the second right.

items.value: The European Union enacted the Nature Restoration Law
items.reasoning: The Nature Restoration Law is European Union legislation, proposed by the European Commission in 2022 and finally adopted by the Council in June 2024 after Parliament's approval. It binds member States to restore degraded ecosystems across a set share of land and sea area, with milestones running to 2030, 2040 and 2050. The World Bank, OECD and FAO are not legislatures and cannot enact binding law of this kind.

items.value: All three statements are not correct — intermediate panchayats are not mandatory in smaller States, the minimum age is twenty-one, and the State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor
items.reasoning: Article 243B carries a proviso that panchayats at the intermediate level need not be constituted in a State with a population not exceeding twenty lakhs, so statement I is wrong. Article 243F sets the qualifying age for membership of a panchayat at not less than twenty-one years, not thirty, so statement II is wrong. Article 243-I places the duty of constituting the Finance Commission to review the financial position of panchayats and recommend the distribution of net proceeds of State taxes on the Governor, not the Chief Minister, so statement III is wrong. Since the question asks which are not correct, the answer covers all three.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — BIMSTEC has seven member States, but it was founded by the Bangkok Declaration of 1997, Nepal is not a founding member, and tourism is not the sub-sector led by India
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct: BIMSTEC's membership stood at seven — Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Statement II is wrong, as the grouping came into being with the Bangkok Declaration of 6 June 1997, not any Dhaka Declaration of 1999. Statement III is wrong because the founding members under that declaration were Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand (as BIST-EC), with Myanmar joining later in 1997 and Nepal and Bhutan only in 2004. Statement IV turns on the sector reallocation adopted with the BIMSTEC Charter, under which the fourteen old sectors were folded into seven pillars and tourism became a sub-sector of the People-to-People Contact pillar led by Nepal, while India leads Security — on that current reading IV is wrong and only I stands. Confidence is low because many secondary accounts still repeat the older fourteen-sector list in which India led tourism; if the paper intended that older structure the answer would be C.

items.value: The Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha are on the Gandhi Peace Prize jury
items.reasoning: The jury for the Gandhi Peace Prize is chaired by the Prime Minister of India and includes the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the single largest opposition party), together with an eminent person nominated for the purpose. The President of India is not a member — the President confers the award but does not sit on the selection jury — which rules out options B and D, and the inclusion of the Chief Justice rules out option A.

items.value: Statements I and II only are correct — GAGAN improves accuracy and integrity and supports better air traffic management, but its benefits are not confined to aviation
items.reasoning: GAGAN is a satellite-based augmentation system built jointly by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India; it uses a network of reference ground stations to compute corrections that improve both the accuracy and the integrity of GPS signals over the Indian region, so statement I is correct. That corrected, certified signal permits precision approaches and more uniform, higher-quality air traffic management, so statement II is correct. Statement III is wrong: GAGAN's corrections are equally usable in railways, road transport, maritime navigation, agriculture, disaster management and personal navigation, so its benefits are not restricted to aviation.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — India co-chaired the Paris AI Action Summit, which followed Bletchley Park and Seoul, but the United States and the United Kingdom refused to sign the declaration
items.reasoning: The AI Action Summit at the Grand Palais in Paris in February 2025 was co-chaired by France and India, and was explicitly presented as the next step after the Bletchley Park summit of 2023 and the Seoul summit of 2024, so statement I is correct. Statement II is wrong: the summit's statement on inclusive and sustainable artificial intelligence for people and the planet was endorsed by around sixty countries including India and China, but the United States and the United Kingdom both declined to sign it, a refusal that was the summit's main headline.

items.value: All four International Year designations are correctly matched to their years
items.reasoning: The United Nations General Assembly has designated 2025 as the International Year of Peace and Trust, 2026 as the International Year of the Woman Farmer, 2027 as the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism, and 2029 as the International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence — the last timed to the close approach of the asteroid Apophis in April 2029. All four rows therefore match. Confidence is moderate rather than high only because the item requires four separate designations to be recalled correctly at once, and the General Assembly often designates several international years for the same calendar year.

items.value: Statements I and II are correct — the 16th BRICS Summit was held at Kazan under Russia's chairship and Indonesia became a full member — but the summit theme was multilateralism, not multiculturalism
items.reasoning: The 16th BRICS Summit was hosted at Kazan in October 2024 under the Russian chairship, so statement I is correct. Indonesia was admitted as a full member with effect from January 2025, announced by Brazil as the incoming chair, so statement II is correct. Statement III substitutes one word: the declared theme was 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security', and multilateralism, not multiculturalism, is the concept BRICS was addressing, so statement III is wrong.

items.value: Only statement III is correct — the minimum age for the Lokpal Chairperson or a Member is forty-five years
items.reasoning: Section 3 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 bars the appointment of any person less than forty-five years of age on the date of assuming office as Chairperson or Member, so statement III is correct. Statement I is wrong because the Act applies to public servants both in and outside India. Statement II is wrong because the Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice of India, a present or former Judge of the Supreme Court, or an eminent person satisfying the specified criteria — the office is not reserved for the Chief Justice alone. Statement IV is wrong because the Lokpal may inquire into allegations against a sitting Prime Minister, subject to safeguards excluding matters of international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space, and requiring approval by a two-thirds majority of the full bench with in-camera proceedings.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — the tournament was held in Delhi, but the two winning margins have been swapped between the men's and women's finals
items.reasoning: The inaugural Kho Kho World Cup was staged in New Delhi in January 2025, so statement I is correct. India beat Nepal in both finals, but the scorelines in statements II and III are interchanged: the 78-40 result belongs to the women's final and the 54-36 result to the men's final, whereas the item attaches 78-40 to the men and 54-36 to the women. Both those statements are therefore wrong as printed and only the first stands. Confidence is moderate because the item turns entirely on recalling two precise scorelines; if the scores were in fact as printed the answer would be D.

items.value: Only statement II is correct — Abhimanyu Mishra of the United States is the youngest ever Grandmaster; Gukesh's title came at the World Championship against Ding Liren, not at the Chess Olympiad against Nepomniachtchi
items.reasoning: Statement I is wrong in almost every particular. The 45th Chess Olympiad at Budapest in 2024 is a team event, which India won in both the open and women's sections; Gukesh Dommaraju became the youngest World Chess Champion separately, by defeating Ding Liren of China in the World Chess Championship match at Singapore in December 2024. Ian Nepomniachtchi was not his opponent in that match. Statement II is correct: Abhimanyu Mishra, an American player, earned the Grandmaster title in 2021 at twelve years and four months, breaking Sergey Karjakin's long-standing record.
